title: Fan Selection Workflow
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: Industrial and Commercial Fans: Fan Selection
description: Clickable twelve-step Mermaid flowchart of the fan selection workflow, from application requirements to the specification, with an eight-card sorting check in which learners assign job information to the step that uses it.
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.
audience: Adult professional development: application engineers, sales staff, representatives, distributors and specifying engineers

educational.subjectArea: Mechanical Engineering / HVAC and Industrial Air Movement
learningObjectives: Classify eight pieces of application information by the selection step that uses them, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a clickable workflow, then classify job information into workflow steps with immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Which selection step consumes this piece of job information?
When a candidate fails the sound or dimension check, which step does the selection loop back to?
Why is the motor sized for the coldest start rather than the hot design temperature?
commonMisconceptions: Selection is finished once a size is read from the performance table.
The motor is sized from the operating brake horsepower at the hot design temperature.
Dimensions are checked only after the order is placed.
assessmentOpportunities: Score of correct first assignments out of 8; mastery is 7 or more.
Follow-up: given a requirement change, name the step the selection loops back to.

dataProvenance: Step order and content from Chapter 27's sections. The 1,450, 1,180 and 1,780 RPM values, the 500°F and 70°F temperatures, the 95 dB limit and the 10 ft by 8 ft pad are the chapter's illustrative worked example.
